detail: CONSERVE HOST_BEAT_TO_REQUEST owner=wb_port lost=28 of=245 from=wb to=req observed=217 | Every host beat the port accepts (wb_cyc_i && wb_stb_i && !wb_stall_o) becomes exactly one request presented to and taken by the command queue (req_valid && req_ready). A port that accepts a beat it cannot deliver has lost a host access: a write is acknowledged and lost, a read is never answered. The port must either stall the beat or hold the request until the queue takes it.

CONSERVE READ_CMD_TO_RESPONSE owner=data_path lost=8 of=64 from=dp_cmd.read to=dp_rd_rsp observed=56 | Every RD command the data path is told about (cmd_rd_valid) yields exactly one read response (rd_rsp_valid), whatever the spacing between RD commands: the spec allows CAS-to-CAS at tCCD, so the capture must pipeline or the command generator must be held, not the command dropped.

CONSERVE WRITE_REQUEST_TO_DATA owner=data_path lost=39 of=153 from=req[we=1] to=dp_wr observed=114 | Every write request the queue takes has its data word accepted by the data path (wr_data_valid && wr_data_ready): the write buffer holds host_interface.write_buffer_depth words and must drain one per WR command issued, so it never refuses a word the queue has already accepted.

CONSERVE WRITE_CMD_TO_BEATS owner=data_path lost=84 of=306 from=dp_cmd.write to=ddr_wr_beat observed=222 per_source=2 | Every WR command drives one full host word onto DQ (host_width_bits / ddr_channel_width_bits beats), whatever the spacing between WR commands (tCCD). A WR command issued to the DRAM without its data writes garbage to the array.
